Surah Al-Mutaffifin (The Defrauders)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Woe﴾ is a mubtada' (subject), its khabar (predicate) being: ﴿to the defrauders﴾, meaning: to those who diminish the rights of people in measuring and weighing.

﴿Alladhina idha iktalu ʿala al-nasi yastawfun﴾ means: when they take measure from people, they take their rights in full, complete. Since their taking of measure from people is a taking that harms them and is applied to them with oppression, he substituted "ʿala" (upon) for "min" (from), to indicate that. It is also permissible for "ʿala" to be connected with "yastawfun", and the object to be placed before the verb, to convey exclusivity, meaning: they take their full due only from people. Al-Farra' said: "min" and "ʿala" alternate in this position, because it is a right upon him (the other party). So when one says "iktaltu ʿalayka" (I took measure upon you), it is as if he said "akhadhtu ma ʿalayka" (I took what is upon you), and when one says "iktaltu minka" (I took measure from you), it is as if he said "istawfaytu minka" (I took my full due from you).

The pronoun in the accusative in ﴿when they measure for them or weigh for them﴾ refers back to the people, meaning "they measure for them" or "they weigh for them." So the preposition is omitted and the verb is made to reach its object directly. The reason it does not say "or when they take measure [from them]" (ittazanu) as it says "or weigh for them" (wazanuhum) is that the meaning is sufficed by the context (iktifa'). It is also possible that the defrauders would not take what is measured and weighed except by measures, because they were able, through the measuring, to achieve full taking (istifa') and theft, since they would shake and trick in the filling. And when they gave, they measured or weighed, because of their ability to cause shortfall (bakhs) in both types.

﴿yukhsirun﴾ means they diminish (yunqisun). It is said: "he made the scale deficient" (khasara al-mizan) and "he made it deficient for him" (akhsarahu).
(p-٦١٤) ﴿Do they not think that they will be raised up (resurrected)?﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 5:

﴿For a great Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. He (God) placed the interrogative hamza (a-, the particle of questioning) before "lā" (the negating particle), as a rebuke. It is not "a-lā" here (in the sense of alerting, al-tanbih), and in it there is denial and great astonishment at their state in daring to commit tatfif (cheating in measure, i.e. giving short weight or measure). It is as if they do not bring it to mind, nor even conjecture that they will be resurrected and called to account for the weight of an atom. Had they believed that they would be resurrected, they would not have short-changed in measure and weight. It is related from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan that a Bedouin (aʿrabi) said to him: "You have heard what God said about those who give short measure" (he meant by this that the one who gives short measure has been threatened with the great threat you have heard of), "so what do you think of yourself, when you take the wealth of the Muslims without measure or weight?!"

"Yawma yaqumu al-nas" (on the Day when mankind stands) is in the accusative, governed by "mab'uthun" (resurrected).

﴿for the Lord of the worlds﴾: that is, for His command and His recompense.

It is related from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he recited this surah, and when he reached this point he wept intensely and refrained from reciting what follows.

Kallā (ﷻ): a rebuke and a warning. That is, He restrains them from what they were engaged in: fraudulent measuring and heedlessness of the Resurrection and the Reckoning. He alerts them that this is something one must repent of and feel remorse over. Then He follows it with a threat against the wicked in general, saying: ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked﴾, that is, the scrolls of their deeds,

﴿is surely in Sijjin﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verses 8–9:

﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ ﴿It is a written register.﴾ If you say: God (Exalted is He) has informed us that the record of the wicked is in Sijjin, and He explained Sijjin as "a written register," so it is as if it were said: "Their record is in a written register." What is its meaning? I say: "Sijjin" is a comprehensive register, the ledger of evil, in which God has recorded the deeds of the devils and the disbelievers, from among the jinn and mankind. It is a written register (marqum), inscribed (mastur), clearly written (bayyin al-kitaba), or marked (mu'lam), so that whoever sees it knows that there is no good in it, from "raqm al-thiyab," meaning its mark or sign. The meaning is that what is written of the deeds of the wicked is recorded in that ledger. It was named "Sijjin," on the pattern of "fi'[ch]il" (fi'
[ʿ]i'īl), derived from "al-sajn," which is confinement and constriction, because it is the cause of confinement and constriction in Hell. Or, because it is cast beneath the seventh earth, in a desolate, dark place, which is the dwelling of Iblis and his offspring. It is a proper noun (ism 'alam) derived from a descriptive term, like "Hatim," and it is diptote (munsarif li-wujud sabab wahid) due to the presence of only one cause, namely being a proper noun alone.

(p-615) ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, the day the written record is brought out,

﴿to the deniers﴾

Those who deny the Day of Judgment, the Recompense and the Reckoning.

Note on the verse: ﴿Those who deny the Day of Judgment﴾

And none deny it except every transgressor (﴿مُعْتَدٍ﴾), one who exceeds the limit, ﴿sinful﴾ (﴿أثِيمٍ﴾), one who earns sin.

Note on the markers: the verse is rendered as "And none deny it except every transgressor, sinful", with the Qur'anic words kept in ﴿ ﴾ as the instructions require.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 13:

﴿When Our verses are recited to him﴾, i.e., the Qur'an,

﴿he says, "Tales of the ancients!"﴾, i.e., the stories of those who came before. Al-Zajjaj said: "Asatir (tales) means falsehoods; its singular is usṭūrah (a tale, a fable), like uḥdūthah (a story), and aḥādīth (narratives)."

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 14:**

﴿Nay!﴾ A rebuke to the transgressor, the sinner, against this saying.

﴿Rather﴾, a negation of what they said. Hafs (one of the transmitters of the Qur'an) pauses on "بَلْ" (bal, "rather"), a brief pause (waqfah, a recitation pause).

﴿Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts.﴾ Their earnings covered them. That is, it prevailed over their hearts until what they used to earn of sins engulfed them. And from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him: "A sin after a sin, until the heart turns black." And from al-Dahhak: "al-Rayn (the covering, rust): the death of the heart." And from Abu Sulayman, may Allah have mercy on him: "al-Rayn and al-qaswah (hardness) are the two reins of heedlessness, and their remedy is persistence in fasting. If hardness is still found after that, let him abandon condiments."

"Kalla" (no! / indeed not): a rebuke against the accumulation (of sins) that has covered their hearts.

"Innahum 'an rabbihim": from seeing their Lord.

"Yawma'idhin lamahjubun": certainly barred, certainly prevented. Al-hajb means prevention (al-man').

Al-Zajjaj said: In the verse there is evidence that the believers will see their Lord, for otherwise the specification would not be meaningful. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "Just as He veiled them in this world from knowing His unity, He veils them in the Hereafter from seeing Him." Malik ibn Anas (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "When He barred His enemies so that they did not see Him, He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him." It has also been said: "from the honour of their Lord," because in this world they did not give thanks for His blessings, so in the Hereafter they are deprived of His honour, as a recompense. The first (view) is more sound, because seeing is the greatest of honours, so being barred from it indicates being barred from everything else.

Then indeed they will be those who roast in the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim), after being veiled from their Lord, [they will be] those who enter the Fire.

Note on the translation: the source text is a short gloss on Qur'an 83:16, and I have rendered it as it stands.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 17:

﴿Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny."﴾ That is: this punishment is what you used to deny in the world, and you used to deny its occurrence.

(p-616) ﴿Kalla﴾: a rebuke against denial.

﴿Inna kitaba al-abrar﴾: what is recorded of their deeds. "Al-abrar" (the righteous) are those who obey, who do not cheat in measure, and who believe in the Resurrection, because it is mentioned in contrast to the wicked (fujjar), and the wicked are explained as those who deny the Day of Judgment. It is reported from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him: "The righteous (al-barr) is one who does not harm even an ant."

﴿La-fi 'Illiyyin﴾: it is a name for the register of good, in which everything that the angels and the righteous of both species (jinn and humans) have done is recorded. It is transferred from the plural of "'Alliyy" (on the pattern "fi'iyyil"), from "al-'uluww" (loftiness). It was so named because it is the cause of rising to the highest ranks in Paradise, or because it is raised up in the seventh heaven, where the Kurubiyyun (angels who are close to the Throne) dwell, as an honour to it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 19:

﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyun is?﴾ That is: what made you know, O Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿what ʿIlliyyun is?﴾ What thing is it?!

Quran 83:21: "Witnessed by those brought near (to Allah)."

Those brought near (al-muqarrabun) attend it: the angels are present at it. It has been said: the muqarrabun of every heaven witness the deeds of the righteous when they are raised up.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 22:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾, enjoying delight in the gardens (al-jinan).

On the couches, [who are] upon couches (al-arā'ik) — the beds, within the canopied enclosures (al-ḥijāl),

﴿looking﴾, at the honour of Allah and His bounties, and at their enemies, how they are being punished.
You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss, the brightness and freshness of enjoyment.

They are given to drink from a sealed wine (raḥīq), a pure drink with no adulteration in it,

﴿sealed﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 26:

﴿Its seal is musk﴾. Its vessels are sealed with musk, in place of the clay with which drinks are sealed in this world. God (Exalted is He) commanded that it be sealed, as an honour to its companions. Or: "Its seal is musk" means its final part has the scent of musk, i.e., the scent of musk is found at the end of its drinking. "Khatamuhu" ("its seal"), "Ali" (the reading attributed to 'Ali),

﴿And for this﴾: that is, for the wine (al-rahiq), or for the bliss (al-na'im),

﴿let those who strive, strive﴾: let those who desire, desire. This only happens through hastening to good deeds and refraining from evil deeds.

(p-617) ﴿And its mixture﴾: the mixture of the sealed wine (al-rahiq).

﴿is of Tasnim﴾: it is a proper name for a specific spring, named "al-Tasnim", which is the verbal noun of "sanamahu" (he raised it), because it is the highest of drinks in Paradise. Or because it comes to them from above and pours into their vessels.

﴿عَيْنًا﴾: it is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative, indicating the state of the noun it modifies), or it is in the *naṣb* (accusative) *ʿalā al-madḥ* (accusative of praise), meaning "a spring" praised for its excellence.

﴿يَشْرَبُ بِها﴾: meaning "from it."

﴿المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾: "those brought near." Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The ones brought near drink it pure, and it is mixed for the companions of the right."

Verse 29 of Surah al-Mutaffifin (83): ﴿Indeed, those who committed crime [were disbelieving]﴾, they disbelieved,

﴿were, of those who believed, laughing﴾, in the world, mocking them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 30:

﴿And when they pass by them, they wink at one another﴾: each of them gestures to the other with the eye, mocking them and finding fault with them. It is said: "'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) came with a group of the Muslims, and the hypocrites mocked them, laughed, winked at one another, and said: 'Look at this bald-headed one!?' So the verse was revealed before 'Ali reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 31:

﴿And when they returned to their own people﴾ meaning: when the disbelievers returned to their homes,

﴿they returned jesting﴾, taking delight in mentioning them and mocking them. And other than Hafs recited "fākihīn" (fākihīn), meaning: rejoicing.

﴿And when they see them﴾, that is, when the disbelievers see the believers,

﴿they say, "Indeed, these are misguided"﴾. That is: Muhammad has deceived these people; they have gone astray, and they have abandoned pleasures for the sake of the honours they hope for in the Hereafter. They have thus forsaken the reality for an illusion, and this is pure misguidance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 33:

﴿And they were not sent as guardians over them﴾, i.e., the disbelievers were not sent as guardians over the believers,

﴿over them﴾, i.e., over the believers,

﴿as guardians﴾, i.e., watching over their states and observing their deeds. Rather, they (the disbelievers) were commanded to reform themselves, so occupying themselves with that is more fitting for them than pursuing others and deriding their intellects (tasfih ahlamihim).
(p. 618) ﴿So today﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾, there, in recompense, just as they laughed at them here.

On the couches they gaze. [This is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl)], meaning: they laugh at them, looking at them and at their state of humiliation and abasement after their former might and arrogance, while they themselves are secure on the couches. It is also said: a door to Paradise is opened for the disbelievers, and it is said to them, "Come (halumma) to Paradise." When they reach it, it is shut in their faces, and the believers laugh at them.
﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?﴾ Have they been repaid for their mockery of the believers in this world, when what was mentioned was done to them?
